item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0024-R02-E018","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Egypt reported constitutional and statutory prohibitions on torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, ratification of relevant international conventions, prison accessibility and health measures, and prosecutorial and Interior Ministry monitoring with criminal or disciplinary referrals for alleged excessive force, torture and harsh treatment.","notes":["The excerpt supports prohibitions on torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, but not the broader attribution of prohibitions on arbitrary detention and abuse as stated.","The excerpt describes government-reported institutional measures and referrals, not el-Sisi's personal supervision or referral outcomes."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0024-R02-E019","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports the reported criminalization and institutional measures, including protections for women and children, trafficking-related offences, disability-related abuse, human-rights sections, sign-language training, and an anti-bullying and anti-violence campaign.","It does not establish reduced violence or consistent enforcement."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0024-R02-E020","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt supports a minimum 5-percent allocation of state-built or state-subsidized housing, monthly assistance and pension-combination rights, accessible transportation and 50-percent fare reductions, and court-approved specially equipped vehicles.","The measures are attributed to laws, ministries and courts rather than directly to el-Sisi, and implementation outcomes are not established."]}]}
